The reset is synchronous, so it is not an asynchronous clear: asserting `reset` between edges does not immediately force `q` to zero. Only at the next rising edge does `reset=1` cause all eight outputs to become zero. A checker that reacts to a mid-cycle reset assertion by zeroing its expected `q` before the next sample will diverge from the hardware.

The second timing fact is that mid-cycle changes to `d` occur after sampling and before the other edge, and they are carried to the start of the next row. This means the checker must distinguish the value of `d` captured at the sampled edge from the value of `d` that will be captured at the next edge.
